---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Altman-Weighted Cheapness
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, at), RATIO(wcap, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Book-to-market earns a premium only when the balance sheet can survive; combining cheapness rank with cumulative-profitability (re/at) and liquidity (wcap/at) ranks isolates cheap-and-solvent firms from cheap-and-failing firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Retained earnings over assets and working capital over assets are the two Altman channels most tied to survival, and both are orthogonal to the price-based valuation channel. Ranking each channel makes the composite robust to outliers and to the negative-equity firms that contaminate raw B/M. The long leg is cheap solvent value; the short leg is expensive firms with depleted equity and negative working capital.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Loss-Persistence Gated Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SIGN(MA(ib, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: A high book-to-market ratio signals a discount for firms with persistently positive earnings but signals impaired asset value (lottery-like distress) for firms with persistent losses, so the value effect should reverse sign across the profitability regime.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The sign flip converts deeply cheap chronic losers from the long leg into the short leg, which is exactly where value strategies historically bleed. Smoothing income over three years prevents a single transitory write-off from misclassifying a healthy firm. This is a genuine interaction because the valuation slope is multiplied by a distress state rather than merely adjusted for it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Net-Debt-Adjusted Operating Yield
EXPRESSION: RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness measured against enterprise value rather than equity value prices the claim of creditors, so firms that look cheap on equity only because they are loaded with net debt no longer screen as cheap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Equity-based multiples mechanically reward leverage, which is precisely the distress channel that makes cheap stocks dangerous; deducting cash and adding debt embeds the distress correction inside the valuation ratio itself. High EBITDA/EV then identifies operating cash generation available to all claimants at a discount. Cash-rich, debt-light cheap firms are ranked most attractive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Coverage-Conditional Sales Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), INDICATOR(RATIO(oancf, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 0.1))
HYPOTHESIS: Sales-to-price identifies revenue bought cheaply, but that revenue is only valuable to shareholders when operating cash flow comfortably services the debt stack; the value signal should be switched off when cash-flow coverage of debt is thin.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Sales-to-price is the value channel least contaminated by accounting losses, so pairing it with a hard cash-flow-to-debt coverage gate cleanly separates cheap operating businesses from cheap leveraged shells. The indicator zeroes out firms whose cash flow covers less than ten percent of total debt, which is where equity is effectively a distressed option. Firms with no debt or ample cash flow retain their full sales-yield score.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Levered Cheapness Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: The joint state of being cheap and highly levered within an industry marks the distressed lottery segment where equity behaves like a deep out-of-the-money option, delivering low average returns despite the apparent discount.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The product of two within-industry ranks is large only in the corner where both cheapness and leverage are extreme, which is the classic value-trap cell that neither theme identifies alone. Industry ranking removes mechanical sector differences in capital structure and typical multiples. Testing this signal with a negative expected sign directly prices the trap side of the economic story.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Deleveraging Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap stocks pay off when the balance sheet is repairing; the same discount alongside rising leverage reflects a firm funding losses with debt and should predict poor returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The level of leverage is slow-moving and largely priced, whereas the annual change in leverage is a timely state variable for whether distress is resolving or intensifying. Multiplying the valuation discount by the deleveraging rate makes the value premium conditional on credit-risk improvement rather than on static solvency. This gives a different mechanism from level-based screens because it captures the direction of the distress process.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Altman-Weighted Cheapness---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially a repackaged value-plus-financial-strength screen (Piotroski/Altman-style quality-value composites are long published), and the nested SUMRANK arbitrarily assigns B/M a 50% weight versus 25% each to the solvency legs without any stated justification, so it is more a known-anomaly blend than a testable cross-theme interaction.

---CRITIQUE Loss-Persistence Gated Value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The sign-flip on three-year smoothed earnings is a genuine interaction rather than a linear control and maps cleanly to the value-trap story, though it is close in spirit to known profitability-conditioned value and the raw unranked B/M ratio (plus negative-ceq firms, which get flipped twice) will make the Fama-MacBeth slope outlier-sensitive.

---CRITIQUE Net-Debt-Adjusted Operating Yield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 1
RATIONALE: EBITDA-to-enterprise-value is the published enterprise multiple anomaly (Loughran-Wellman 2011) verbatim, and it is a single ratio with no cross-theme interaction at all.

---CRITIQUE Coverage-Conditional Sales Yield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Internally inconsistent: the reasoning claims "firms with no debt retain their full sales-yield score," but with dltt+dlc = 0 the coverage ratio is undefined and those firms will be dropped or mis-gated, and the underlying sales-to-price leg is itself a long-published value anomaly attached to a lossy hard 0/1 switch.

---CRITIQUE Levered Cheapness Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The expected negative sign fights the expression's dominant loading — the product of two positive ranks is monotone increasing in B/M, so the signal will largely inherit the positive value premium — and the low end of a rank product is an ambiguous mixture of cheap-unlevered and expensive-levered firms, making the short leg economically ill-defined and the construct close to the known distress anomaly.

---CRITIQUE Deleveraging Value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Conditioning the value discount on the direction rather than the level of leverage is a defensible and reasonably distinct mechanism, but the unranked product will be dominated by the magnitude of the noisy annual leverage change rather than by cheapness, so a rank-by-rank or sign-gated version would likely be needed for the portfolio evidence to be stable.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Weakest-Link Cheap And Solvent
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(re, che), lt), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: A stock is a compensated value opportunity only if it clears both hurdles simultaneously; the payoff is governed by the binding constraint, so the relevant score is the minimum of within-industry cheapness rank and within-industry solvency-buffer rank (retained earnings plus cash minus total liabilities, scaled by assets).
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: MIN is a conjunctive, non-additive interaction that replaces the arbitrary 50/25/25 weighting of the earlier nested SUMRANK — no fixed weights are imposed and a high score is unattainable by excelling on one theme alone. The short leg is economically coherent rather than a mixture of good states: a low minimum means the firm is either richly priced or has an eroded solvency buffer, both of which carry low expected returns, whereas the earlier rank-product's low end contained attractive cheap-unlevered firms.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Rollover-Gap Weighted Earnings Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), at), 2))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness is rewarded only when the firm does not face a near-term refinancing wall; the same earnings yield is a trap when maturing short-term debt exceeds cash on hand, because equity holders bear the rollover option's downside.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the published enterprise-multiple ratio entirely and instead makes the valuation slope a function of a specific, timing-based distress state — cash minus debt in current liabilities — so the signal flips sign across the funding-gap boundary rather than merely re-scaling price by leverage. Using a percentile rank for the earnings-yield leg keeps that leg non-negative, so the sign is set by the rollover gap and the magnitude by cheapness, avoiding the perverse quadrant where a loss-making firm with a maturity wall would score positively. The gap is defined for every firm including debt-free ones (dlc = 0 simply yields cash-to-assets), so no observations are dropped or mis-gated.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cash-Burn Persistence Weighted Sales Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(oancf, 0), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(oancf), 0), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Revenue bought cheaply is valuable when the business has consistently self-funded, and is a distressed-lottery claim when the same revenue has been produced alongside repeated years of negative operating cash flow; the value slope should therefore scale with the net count of self-funding years over the last five.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This removes the ill-defined coverage denominator that broke on zero-debt firms — the multiplier only needs the sign of operating cash flow, which exists for every reporting firm — and it replaces the lossy 0/1 switch with a graded score running from -5 to +5, so the short leg is cheap chronic cash burners rather than a discarded subsample. Persistence over five years, rather than a one-year snapshot, is the economically correct distress state because a single negative cash-flow year is often investment-driven while five are a solvency verdict. Expensively priced firms receive a small sales yield and therefore sit near the middle regardless of their burn history, so the spread is driven by the interaction rather than by either theme alone.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Distress Sorted Within Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), NEG(RATIO(oancf, lt)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The value-trap effect is a within-value phenomenon: conditional on being in the cheapest 30% of the cross-section, higher leverage and weaker cash-flow coverage of liabilities identify firms whose discount reflects impaired solvency, and those firms underperform the healthy cheap firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Restricting the distress score to the cheap bucket and centering it removes the dominant monotone B/M loading that made the earlier rank product simply re-express the value premium — value stocks now populate both tails of the signal, so the spread is purely the distress gradient inside cheapness. Both legs are economically explicit: the short leg is cheap and highly levered with weak operating cash flow relative to liabilities, the long leg is cheap with low liabilities and strong cash coverage, and non-value firms sit at zero in the middle rather than contaminating either extreme. This is a conditional distress sort, not the unconditional distress anomaly, because the same distress score is switched off outside the value region.
REASONING_END
